summary: DeepXube is a free and open-source Python package and command-line tool that seeks to automate the solution of pathfinding problems by using machine learning to learn heuristic functions that guide heuristic search algorithms tailored to deep neural networks (DNNs). DeepXube is comprised of the latest advances in deep reinforcement learning, heuristic search, and formal logic for solving pathfinding problems. This includes limited-horizon Bellman-based learning, hindsight experience replay, batched heuristic search, and specifying goals with answer-set programming. A robust multiple-inheritance structure simplifies the definition of pathfinding domains and the generation of training data. Training heuristic functions is made efficient through the automatic parallelization of the generation of training data across central processing units (CPUs) and reinforcement learning updates across graphics processing units (GPUs). Pathfinding algorithms that take advantage of the parallelism of GPUs and DNN architectures, such as batch weighted A* and Q* search and beam search are easily employed to solve pathfinding problems through command-line arguments. Finally, several convenient features for visualization, code profiling, and progress monitoring during training and solving are available. The GitHub repository is publicly available at https://github.com/forestagostinelli/deepxube.

AI.tldr: DeepXube is an open-source Python package that automates pathfinding problem solving using machine-learned heuristic functions, combining deep reinforcement learning, heuristic search, and formal logic with efficient GPU/CPU parallelization.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to automate the solution of pathfinding problems by leveraging machine learning to learn heuristic functions, making heuristic search more accessible and efficient for complex domains, particularly those involving deep neural networks.
AI.method: DeepXube combines deep reinforcement learning (limited-horizon Bellman-based learning, hindsight experience replay), heuristic search algorithms (batch weighted A*, Q* search, beam search), and formal logic (answer-set programming for goal specification). It features a multiple-inheritance structure for domain definition and automatic parallelization of training data generation across CPUs and reinforcement learning updates across GPUs.
AI.result: The result is a publicly available open-source tool (GitHub repository) that provides efficient pathfinding automation with visualization, code profiling, and progress monitoring features, enabling users to easily apply advanced heuristic search techniques to complex problems.
AI.conclusion: DeepXube successfully integrates state-of-the-art techniques from multiple fields to create a comprehensive, efficient, and user-friendly tool for automating pathfinding problem solving through learned heuristic functions and parallelized computation.

title: SOMA: Strategic Orchestration and Memory-Augmented System for Vision-Language-Action Model Robustness via In-Context Adaptation
comment: 9 pages, 16 figures, 3 table. Submitted to IROS 2026
summary: Despite the promise of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models as generalist robotic controllers, their robustness against perceptual noise and environmental variations in out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks remains fundamentally limited by the absence of long-term memory, causal failure attribution, and dynamic intervention capability. To address this, we propose SOMA, a Strategic Orchestration and Memory-Augmented System that upgrades frozen VLA policies for robust in-context adaptation without parameter fine-tuning. Specifically, SOMA operates through an online pipeline of contrastive Dual-Memory Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), an Attribution-Driven Large-Language-Model (LLM) Orchestrator, and extensible Model Context Protocol (MCP) interventions, while an offline Memory Consolidation module continuously distills the execution traces into reliable priors. Experimental evaluations across three backbone models (pi0, pi0.5, and SmolVLA) on LIBERO-PRO and our proposed LIBERO-SOMA benchmarks demonstrate that SOMA achieves an average absolute success rate gain of 56.6%. This includes a significant absolute improvement of 89.1% in long-horizon task chaining. Project page and source code are available at: https://github.com/LZY-1021/SOMA.

AI.tldr: SOMA is a memory-augmented system that enhances frozen Vision-Language-Action models for robust robotic control by adding long-term memory, causal failure attribution, and dynamic intervention capabilities without parameter fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models lack robustness against perceptual noise and environmental variations in out-of-distribution tasks due to absence of long-term memory, causal failure attribution, and dynamic intervention capabilities.
AI.method: SOMA uses an online pipeline with contrastive Dual-Memory Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Attribution-Driven LLM Orchestrator, and extensible Model Context Protocol (MCP) interventions, plus an offline Memory Consolidation module that distills execution traces into reliable priors.
AI.result: SOMA achieves an average absolute success rate gain of 56.6% across three backbone models (pi0, pi0.5, and SmolVLA) on LIBERO-PRO and LIBERO-SOMA benchmarks, with 89.1% absolute improvement in long-horizon task chaining.
AI.conclusion: SOMA effectively upgrades frozen VLA policies for robust in-context adaptation without parameter fine-tuning, addressing key limitations in current VLA models through strategic orchestration and memory augmentation.

title: DUPLEX: Agentic Dual-System Planning via LLM-Driven Information Extraction
summary: While Large Language Models (LLMs) provide semantic flexibility for robotic task planning, their susceptibility to hallucination and logical inconsistency limits their reliability in long-horizon domains. To bridge the gap between unstructured environments and rigorous plan synthesis, we propose DUPLEX, an agentic dual-system neuro-symbolic architecture that strictly confines the LLM to schema-guided information extraction rather than end-to-end planning or code generation. In our framework, a feed-forward Fast System utilizes a lightweight LLM to extract entities, relations etc. from natural language, deterministically mapping them into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) problem file for a classical symbolic planner. To resolve complex or underspecified scenarios, a Slow System is activated exclusively upon planning failure, leveraging solver diagnostics to drive a high-capacity LLM in iterative reflection and repair. Extensive evaluations across 12 classical and household planning domains demonstrate that DUPLEX significantly outperforms existing end-to-end and hybrid LLM baselines in both success rate and reliability. These results confirm that The key is not to make the LLM plan better, but to restrict the LLM to the part it is good at - structured semantic grounding - and leave logical plan synthesis to a symbolic planner.

AI.tldr: DUPLEX is a dual-system neuro-symbolic architecture that restricts LLMs to schema-guided information extraction while using symbolic planners for logical plan synthesis, achieving superior reliability in robotic task planning.
AI.motivation: LLMs offer semantic flexibility for robotic task planning but suffer from hallucination and logical inconsistency, limiting reliability in long-horizon domains. There's a need to bridge unstructured environments with rigorous plan synthesis.
AI.method: DUPLEX uses a dual-system architecture: 1) Fast System: lightweight LLM extracts entities/relations from natural language and deterministically maps them to PDDL problem files for classical symbolic planners; 2) Slow System: activated only upon planning failure, uses solver diagnostics to drive high-capacity LLM in iterative reflection and repair.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations across 12 classical and household planning domains show DUPLEX significantly outperforms existing end-to-end and hybrid LLM baselines in both success rate and reliability.
AI.conclusion: The key insight is not to make LLMs plan better, but to restrict them to structured semantic grounding (what they're good at) while leaving logical plan synthesis to symbolic planners.

title: AnalogAgent: Self-Improving Analog Circuit Design Automation with LLM Agents
summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) suggest strong potential for automating analog circuit design. Yet most LLM-based approaches rely on a single-model loop of generation, diagnosis, and correction, which favors succinct summaries over domain-specific insight and suffers from context attrition that erases critical technical details. To address these limitations, we propose AnalogAgent, a training-free agentic framework that integrates an LLM-based multi-agent system (MAS) with self-evolving memory (SEM) for analog circuit design automation. AnalogAgent coordinates a Code Generator, Design Optimizer, and Knowledge Curator to distill execution feedback into an adaptive playbook in SEM and retrieve targeted guidance for subsequent generation, enabling cross-task transfer without additional expert feedback, databases, or libraries. Across established benchmarks, AnalogAgent achieves 92% Pass@1 with Gemini and 97.4% Pass@1 with GPT-5. Moreover, with compact models (e.g., Qwen-8B), it yields a +48.8% average Pass@1 gain across tasks and reaches 72.1% Pass@1 overall, indicating that AnalogAgent substantially strengthens open-weight models for high-quality analog circuit design automation.

AI.tldr: AnalogAgent: A training-free multi-agent framework with self-evolving memory for analog circuit design automation, achieving high Pass@1 rates across benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Current LLM-based approaches for analog circuit design rely on single-model loops that favor summaries over domain-specific insight and suffer from context attrition, erasing critical technical details.
AI.method: Proposes AnalogAgent, a training-free agentic framework integrating an LLM-based multi-agent system (MAS) with self-evolving memory (SEM). Coordinates Code Generator, Design Optimizer, and Knowledge Curator to distill execution feedback into adaptive playbook in SEM and retrieve targeted guidance.
AI.result: Achieves 92% Pass@1 with Gemini and 97.4% Pass@1 with GPT-5. With compact models (Qwen-8B), yields +48.8% average Pass@1 gain across tasks and reaches 72.1% Pass@1 overall.
AI.conclusion: AnalogAgent substantially strengthens open-weight models for high-quality analog circuit design automation, enabling cross-task transfer without additional expert feedback, databases, or libraries.

title: Equivariant Filter Transformations for Consistent and Efficient Visual--Inertial Navigation
summary: This paper presents an equivariant filter (EqF) transformation approach for visual--inertial navigation. By establishing analytical links between EqFs with different symmetries, the proposed approach enables systematic consistency design and efficient implementation. First, we formalize the mapping from the global system state to the local error-state and prove that it induces a nonsingular linear transformation between the error-states of any two EqFs. Second, we derive transformation laws for the associated linearized error-state systems and unobservable subspaces. These results yield a general consistency design principle: for any unobservable system, a consistent EqF with a state-independent unobservable subspace can be synthesized by transforming the local coordinate chart, thereby avoiding ad hoc symmetry analysis. Third, to mitigate the computational burden arising from the non-block-diagonal Jacobians required for consistency, we propose two efficient implementation strategies. These strategies exploit the Jacobians of a simpler EqF with block-diagonal structure to accelerate covariance operations while preserving consistency. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and real-world experiments validate the proposed approach in terms of both accuracy and runtime.

AI.tldr: Equivariant filter transformation approach for visual-inertial navigation that enables systematic consistency design and efficient implementation through analytical links between filters with different symmetries.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the need for systematic consistency design in equivariant filters for visual-inertial navigation, avoiding ad hoc symmetry analysis, while also mitigating computational burdens from non-block-diagonal Jacobians required for consistency.
AI.method: 1) Formalizes mapping from global system state to local error-state and proves it induces nonsingular linear transformation between error-states of any two EqFs. 2) Derives transformation laws for linearized error-state systems and unobservable subspaces. 3) Proposes two efficient implementation strategies that exploit Jacobians of simpler EqF with block-diagonal structure to accelerate covariance operations while preserving consistency.
AI.result: Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and real-world experiments validate the proposed approach in terms of both accuracy and runtime, demonstrating effective consistency design and computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: The proposed equivariant filter transformation approach provides a general consistency design principle and efficient implementation strategies for visual-inertial navigation, enabling systematic filter synthesis without ad hoc symmetry analysis while maintaining computational efficiency.

title: From Pixels to Digital Agents: An Empirical Study on the Taxonomy and Technological Trends of Reinforcement Learning Environments
summary: The remarkable progress of reinforcement learning (RL) is intrinsically tied to the environments used to train and evaluate artificial agents. Moving beyond traditional qualitative reviews, this work presents a large-scale, data-driven empirical investigation into the evolution of RL environments. By programmatically processing a massive corpus of academic literature and rigorously distilling over 2,000 core publications, we propose a quantitative methodology to map the transition from isolated physical simulations to generalist, language-driven foundation agents. Implementing a novel, multi-dimensional taxonomy, we systematically analyze benchmarks against diverse application domains and requisite cognitive capabilities. Our automated semantic and statistical analysis reveals a profound, data-verified paradigm shift: the bifurcation of the field into a "Semantic Prior" ecosystem dominated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and a "Domain-Specific Generalization" ecosystem. Furthermore, we characterize the "cognitive fingerprints" of these distinct domains to uncover the underlying mechanisms of cross-task synergy, multi-domain interference, and zero-shot generalization. Ultimately, this study offers a rigorous, quantitative roadmap for designing the next generation of Embodied Semantic Simulators, bridging the gap between continuous physical control and high-level logical reasoning.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a large-scale empirical analysis of RL environment evolution, revealing a paradigm shift toward two distinct ecosystems: "Semantic Prior" (LLM-dominated) and "Domain-Specific Generalization," with implications for designing next-generation embodied semantic simulators.
AI.motivation: To move beyond qualitative reviews and provide a data-driven understanding of how reinforcement learning environments have evolved, particularly in relation to the transition from isolated physical simulations to generalist, language-driven foundation agents.
AI.method: Programmatic processing of a massive corpus of academic literature (over 2,000 core publications) using quantitative methodology, implementing a novel multi-dimensional taxonomy, and conducting automated semantic and statistical analysis to map environment evolution.
AI.result: Reveals a profound paradigm shift: bifurcation into "Semantic Prior" ecosystem (dominated by LLMs) and "Domain-Specific Generalization" ecosystem, with characterization of "cognitive fingerprints" uncovering mechanisms of cross-task synergy, multi-domain interference, and zero-shot generalization.
AI.conclusion: Provides a rigorous, quantitative roadmap for designing next-generation Embodied Semantic Simulators that bridge the gap between continuous physical control and high-level logical reasoning.

title: Accelerated Spline-Based Time-Optimal Motion Planning with Continuous Safety Guarantees for Non-Differentially Flat Systems
comment: Submitted to the 2026 10th IEEE Conference on Control Technology and Applications (CCTA)
summary: Generating time-optimal, collision-free trajectories for autonomous mobile robots involves a fundamental trade-off between guaranteeing safety and managing computational complexity. State-of-the-art approaches formulate spline-based motion planning as a single Optimal Control Problem (OCP) but often suffer from high computational cost because they include separating hyperplane parameters as decision variables to enforce continuous collision avoidance. This paper presents a novel method that alleviates this bottleneck by decoupling the determination of separating hyperplanes from the OCP. By treating the separation theorem as an independent classification problem solvable via a linear system or quadratic program, the proposed method eliminates hyperplane parameters from the optimisation variables, effectively transforming non-convex constraints into linear ones. Experimental validation demonstrates that this decoupled approach reduces trajectory computation times up to almost 60% compared to fully coupled methods in obstacle-rich environments, while maintaining rigorous continuous safety guarantees.

AI.tldr: Decoupling separating hyperplanes from optimal control reduces computation time by ~60% while maintaining safety for robot motion planning.
AI.motivation: Existing spline-based motion planning methods suffer from high computational cost because they include separating hyperplane parameters as decision variables in a single Optimal Control Problem (OCP) for continuous collision avoidance.
AI.method: Decouples determination of separating hyperplanes from the OCP by treating the separation theorem as an independent classification problem solvable via linear system or quadratic program, eliminating hyperplane parameters from optimization variables and transforming non-convex constraints into linear ones.
AI.result: Experimental validation shows the decoupled approach reduces trajectory computation times up to almost 60% compared to fully coupled methods in obstacle-rich environments while maintaining rigorous continuous safety guarantees.
AI.conclusion: The proposed decoupling method effectively addresses the computational bottleneck in time-optimal, collision-free trajectory planning for autonomous mobile robots by separating hyperplane determination from the optimization problem.

title: Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Planning for Personalized and Fair Participatory Urban Sensing
summary: Participatory urban sensing leverages human mobility for large-scale urban data collection, yet existing methods typically rely on centralized optimization and assume homogeneous participants, resulting in rigid assignments that overlook personal preferences and heterogeneous urban contexts. We propose MAPUS, an LLM-based multi-agent framework for personalized and fair participatory urban sensing. In our framework, participants are modeled as autonomous agents with individual profiles and schedules, while a coordinator agent performs fairness-aware selection and refines sensing routes through language-based negotiation. Experiments on real-world datasets show that MAPUS achieves competitive sensing coverage while substantially improving participant satisfaction and fairness, promoting more human-centric and sustainable urban sensing systems.

AI.tldr: MAPUS is an LLM-based multi-agent framework that improves participatory urban sensing by modeling participants as autonomous agents with individual preferences and using language-based negotiation for fair, personalized task assignments.
AI.motivation: Existing participatory urban sensing methods rely on centralized optimization and assume homogeneous participants, resulting in rigid assignments that overlook personal preferences and heterogeneous urban contexts, leading to poor participant satisfaction and fairness.
AI.method: MAPUS uses an LLM-based multi-agent framework where participants are modeled as autonomous agents with individual profiles and schedules. A coordinator agent performs fairness-aware selection and refines sensing routes through language-based negotiation between agents.
AI.result: Experiments on real-world datasets show that MAPUS achieves competitive sensing coverage while substantially improving participant satisfaction and fairness compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: MAPUS promotes more human-centric and sustainable urban sensing systems by addressing the limitations of traditional centralized approaches through personalized, fairness-aware multi-agent coordination.

title: Goal-Oriented Reactive Simulation for Closed-Loop Trajectory Prediction
summary: Current trajectory prediction models are primarily trained in an open-loop manner, which often leads to covariate shift and compounding errors when deployed in real-world, closed-loop settings. Furthermore, relying on static datasets or non-reactive log-replay simulators severs the interactive loop, preventing the ego agent from learning to actively negotiate surrounding traffic. In this work, we propose an on-policy closed-loop training paradigm optimized for high-frequency, receding horizon ego prediction. To ground the ego prediction in a realistic representation of traffic interactions and to achieve reactive consistency, we introduce a goal-oriented, transformer-based scene decoder, resulting in an inherently reactive training simulation. By exposing the ego agent to a mixture of open-loop data and simulated, self-induced states, the model learns recovery behaviors to correct its own execution errors. Extensive evaluation demonstrates that closed-loop training significantly enhances collision avoidance capabilities at high replanning frequencies, yielding relative collision rate reductions of up to 27.0% on nuScenes and 79.5% in dense DeepScenario intersections compared to open-loop baselines. Additionally, we show that a hybrid simulation combining reactive with non-reactive surrounding agents achieves optimal balance between immediate interactivity and long-term behavioral stability.

AI.tldr: Closed-loop training paradigm for trajectory prediction improves collision avoidance by enabling ego agents to learn recovery behaviors through reactive simulation.
AI.motivation: Current open-loop training causes covariate shift and compounding errors in real-world deployment, and static datasets prevent learning interactive negotiation with traffic.
AI.method: On-policy closed-loop training with goal-oriented transformer-based scene decoder for reactive simulation, mixing open-loop data with self-induced states.
AI.result: 27.0% collision rate reduction on nuScenes, 79.5% reduction in dense DeepScenario intersections; hybrid simulation balances interactivity and stability.
AI.conclusion: Closed-loop training significantly enhances collision avoidance at high replanning frequencies by enabling learning of recovery behaviors through reactive simulation.

title: ELITE: Experiential Learning and Intent-Aware Transfer for Self-improving Embodied Agents
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown remarkable general capabilities, yet embodied agents built on them fail at complex tasks, often skipping critical steps, proposing invalid actions, and repeating mistakes. These failures arise from a fundamental gap between the static training data of VLMs and the physical interaction for embodied tasks. VLMs can learn rich semantic knowledge from static data but lack the ability to interact with the world. To address this issue, we introduce ELITE, an embodied agent framework with {E}xperiential {L}earning and {I}ntent-aware {T}ransfer that enables agents to continuously learn from their own environment interaction experiences, and transfer acquired knowledge to procedurally similar tasks. ELITE operates through two synergistic mechanisms, \textit{i.e.,} self-reflective knowledge construction and intent-aware retrieval. Specifically, self-reflective knowledge construction extracts reusable strategies from execution trajectories and maintains an evolving strategy pool through structured refinement operations. Then, intent-aware retrieval identifies relevant strategies from the pool and applies them to current tasks. Experiments on the EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat benchmarks show that ELITE achieves 9\% and 5\% performance improvement over base VLMs in the online setting without any supervision. In the supervised setting, ELITE generalizes effectively to unseen task categories, achieving better performance compared to state-of-the-art training-based methods. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of ELITE for bridging the gap between semantic understanding and reliable action execution.

AI.tldr: ELITE is an embodied agent framework with experiential learning and intent-aware transfer that enables agents to learn from environment interactions and transfer knowledge to similar tasks, addressing the gap between VLMs' semantic understanding and reliable action execution.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models (VLMs) have strong general capabilities but fail at complex embodied tasks due to a fundamental gap between static training data and physical interaction requirements. Embodied agents built on VLMs often skip critical steps, propose invalid actions, and repeat mistakes.
AI.method: ELITE operates through two synergistic mechanisms: 1) Self-reflective knowledge construction that extracts reusable strategies from execution trajectories and maintains an evolving strategy pool through structured refinement operations, and 2) Intent-aware retrieval that identifies relevant strategies from the pool and applies them to current tasks.
AI.result: Experiments on EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat benchmarks show ELITE achieves 9% and 5% performance improvement over base VLMs in online settings without supervision. In supervised settings, ELITE generalizes effectively to unseen task categories, achieving better performance than state-of-the-art training-based methods.
AI.conclusion: ELITE effectively bridges the gap between semantic understanding and reliable action execution by enabling continuous learning from environment interactions and knowledge transfer to procedurally similar tasks.

title: Environment-Grounded Multi-Agent Workflow for Autonomous Penetration Testing
summary: The increasing complexity and interconnectivity of digital infrastructures make scalable and reliable security assessment methods essential. Robotic systems represent a particularly important class of operational technology, as modern robots are highly networked cyber-physical systems deployed in domains such as industrial automation, logistics, and autonomous services. This paper explores the use of large language models for automated penetration testing in robotic environments. We propose an environment-grounded multi-agent architecture tailored to Robotics-based systems. The approach dynamically constructs a shared graph-based memory during execution that captures the observable system state, including network topology, communication channels, vulnerabilities, and attempted exploits. This enables structured automation while maintaining traceability and effective context management throughout the testing process. Evaluated across multiple iterations within a specialized robotics Capture-the-Flag scenario (ROS/ROS2), the system demonstrated high reliability, successfully completing the challenge in 100\% of test runs (n=5). This performance significantly exceeds literature benchmarks while maintaining the traceability and human oversight required by frameworks like the EU AI Act.

AI.tldr: LLM-based multi-agent system for automated penetration testing in robotic environments using graph-based memory to track system state and exploits, achieving 100% success rate in ROS/ROS2 CTF scenarios.
AI.motivation: Increasing complexity of digital infrastructures requires scalable security assessment methods, with robotic systems being critical cyber-physical systems in industrial automation, logistics, and autonomous services that need robust security testing.
AI.method: Environment-grounded multi-agent architecture using large language models for robotic penetration testing, featuring dynamic construction of shared graph-based memory that captures network topology, communication channels, vulnerabilities, and attempted exploits for structured automation with traceability.
AI.result: System demonstrated high reliability with 100% success rate (n=5) in specialized robotics Capture-the-Flag scenarios (ROS/ROS2), significantly exceeding literature benchmarks while maintaining traceability and human oversight requirements.
AI.conclusion: LLM-based multi-agent approach provides effective automated penetration testing for robotic environments, achieving superior performance while meeting regulatory compliance requirements like the EU AI Act through maintained traceability and oversight.

title: Enhanced Mycelium of Thought (EMoT): A Bio-Inspired Hierarchical Reasoning Architecture with Strategic Dormancy and Mnemonic Encoding
comment: 32 pages, 6 figures, 15 tables; includes ablation studies and reasoning trace visualisation
summary: Current prompting paradigms for large language models (LLMs), including Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT), follow linear or tree-structured reasoning paths that lack persistent memory, strategic dormancy, and cross-domain synthesis. We present the Enhanced Mycelium of Thought (EMoT) framework, a bio-inspired reasoning architecture that organises cognitive processing into a four-level hierarchy (Micro, Meso, Macro, Meta), implements strategic dormancy and reactivation of reasoning nodes, and integrates a Memory Palace with five mnemonic encoding styles. EMoT is a research prototype for complex, multi-domain problems, not a general-purpose prompting enhancement. Two complementary evaluations reveal a characteristic trade-off. In a blind LLM-as-Judge evaluation across three domains, EMoT achieved near-parity with CoT (4.20 vs. 4.33/5.0) with higher stability, and outperformed CoT on Cross-Domain Synthesis (4.8 vs. 4.4). Ablation studies show that strategic dormancy is architecturally essential (quality collapsed from 4.2 to 1.0 when disabled). On a 15-item short-answer benchmark, EMoT (27%) substantially underperformed simpler baselines, confirming systematic overthinking on simple problems. These results are subject to important limitations: small sample sizes (n=3 complex cases, n=15 short-answer items), LLM-as-Judge evaluation with potential self-preference bias, and approximately 33-fold computational cost overhead. To our knowledge, EMoT is the first reasoning framework to combine hierarchical topology, strategic thought dormancy with reactivation, and mnemonic memory encoding in a single architecture.

AI.tldr: EMoT is a bio-inspired reasoning framework with hierarchical structure, strategic dormancy, and mnemonic memory encoding that shows trade-offs: performs well on complex cross-domain problems but overthinks simple tasks with high computational cost.
AI.motivation: Current LLM prompting paradigms (CoT, ToT) lack persistent memory, strategic dormancy, and cross-domain synthesis capabilities, limiting their effectiveness for complex, multi-domain reasoning problems.
AI.method: EMoT organizes cognitive processing into a four-level hierarchy (Micro, Meso, Macro, Meta), implements strategic dormancy/reactivation of reasoning nodes, and integrates a Memory Palace with five mnemonic encoding styles.
AI.result: EMoT achieved near-parity with CoT (4.20 vs. 4.33/5.0) with higher stability, outperformed CoT on Cross-Domain Synthesis (4.8 vs. 4.4), but substantially underperformed simpler baselines on simple problems (27% vs. better baselines). Strategic dormancy was essential (quality collapsed from 4.2 to 1.0 when disabled).
AI.conclusion: EMoT demonstrates a characteristic trade-off: effective for complex, multi-domain problems but systematically overthinks simple tasks, with significant computational overhead (33× cost). It represents the first framework combining hierarchical topology, strategic dormancy with reactivation, and mnemonic memory encoding.

title: Decentralized End-to-End Multi-AAV Pursuit Using Predictive Spatio-Temporal Observation via Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Decentralized cooperative pursuit in cluttered environments is challenging for autonomous aerial swarms, especially under partial and noisy perception. Existing methods often rely on abstracted geometric features or privileged ground-truth states, and therefore sidestep perceptual uncertainty in real-world settings. We propose a decentralized end-to-end multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that maps raw LiDAR observations directly to continuous control commands. Central to the framework is the Predictive Spatio-Temporal Observation (PSTO), an egocentric grid representation that aligns obstacle geometry with predictive adversarial intent and teammate motion in a unified, fixed-resolution projection. Built on PSTO, a single decentralized policy enables agents to navigate static obstacles, intercept dynamic targets, and maintain cooperative encirclement. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior capture efficiency and competitive success rates compared to state-of-the-art learning-based approaches relying on privileged obstacle information. Furthermore, the unified policy scales seamlessly across different team sizes without retraining. Finally, fully autonomous outdoor experiments validate the framework on a quadrotor swarm relying on only onboard sensing and computing.

AI.tldr: Decentralized MARL framework for aerial swarm pursuit using raw LiDAR and predictive spatio-temporal observations to handle obstacles, dynamic targets, and cooperative encirclement without privileged information.
AI.motivation: Existing decentralized pursuit methods for aerial swarms often rely on abstracted geometric features or privileged ground-truth states, sidestepping real-world perceptual uncertainty from partial and noisy sensing in cluttered environments.
AI.method: Proposes a decentralized end-to-end MARL framework that maps raw LiDAR observations directly to continuous control commands. Key innovation is Predictive Spatio-Temporal Observation (PSTO) - an egocentric grid representation aligning obstacle geometry with predictive adversarial intent and teammate motion in unified fixed-resolution projection. Single decentralized policy enables navigation of static obstacles, interception of dynamic targets, and cooperative encirclement.
AI.result: Superior capture efficiency and competitive success rates compared to state-of-the-art learning-based approaches relying on privileged obstacle information. Unified policy scales seamlessly across different team sizes without retraining. Validated through fully autonomous outdoor experiments on quadrotor swarm using only onboard sensing and computing.
AI.conclusion: The PSTO-based MARL framework effectively addresses decentralized cooperative pursuit in cluttered environments under partial/noisy perception, demonstrating practical applicability through successful real-world deployment on aerial swarms with onboard sensing.

title: Bridging the Evaluation Gap: Standardized Benchmarks for Multi-Objective Search
summary: Empirical evaluation in multi-objective search (MOS) has historically suffered from fragmentation, relying on heterogeneous problem instances with incompatible objective definitions that make cross-study comparisons difficult. This standardization gap is further exacerbated by the realization that DIMACS road networks, a historical default benchmark for the field, exhibit highly correlated objectives that fail to capture diverse Pareto-front structures. To address this, we introduce the first comprehensive, standardized benchmark suite for exact and approximate MOS. Our suite spans four structurally diverse domains: real-world road networks, structured synthetic graphs, game-based grid environments, and high-dimensional robotic motion-planning roadmaps. By providing fixed graph instances, standardized start-goal queries, and both exact and approximate reference Pareto-optimal solution sets, this suite captures a full spectrum of objective interactions: from strongly correlated to strictly independent. Ultimately, this benchmark provides a common foundation to ensure future MOS evaluations are robust, reproducible, and structurally comprehensive.

AI.tldr: First comprehensive standardized benchmark suite for multi-objective search addressing fragmentation in empirical evaluation by providing diverse domains with fixed instances and standardized queries.
AI.motivation: Multi-objective search evaluation suffers from fragmentation due to heterogeneous problem instances with incompatible objective definitions, making cross-study comparisons difficult. DIMACS road networks, the historical default benchmark, exhibit highly correlated objectives that fail to capture diverse Pareto-front structures.
AI.method: Introduce a comprehensive benchmark suite spanning four structurally diverse domains: real-world road networks, structured synthetic graphs, game-based grid environments, and high-dimensional robotic motion-planning roadmaps. Provide fixed graph instances, standardized start-goal queries, and both exact and approximate reference Pareto-optimal solution sets.
AI.result: The benchmark suite captures a full spectrum of objective interactions: from strongly correlated to strictly independent, addressing the limitations of previous benchmarks that only represented highly correlated objectives.
AI.conclusion: This benchmark provides a common foundation to ensure future multi-objective search evaluations are robust, reproducible, and structurally comprehensive, addressing the standardization gap in the field.

title: Toward Generalist Neural Motion Planners for Robotic Manipulators: Challenges and Opportunities
summary: State-of-the-art generalist manipulation policies have enabled the deployment of robotic manipulators in unstructured human environments. However, these frameworks struggle in cluttered environments primarily because they utilize auxiliary modules for low-level motion planning and control. Motion planning remains challenging due to the high dimensionality of the robot's configuration space and the presence of workspace obstacles. Neural motion planners have enhanced motion planning efficiency by offering fast inference and effectively handling the inherent multi-modality of the motion planning problem. Despite such benefits, current neural motion planners often struggle to generalize to unseen, out-of-distribution planning settings. This paper reviews and analyzes the state-of-the-art neural motion planners, highlighting both their benefits and limitations. It also outlines a path toward establishing generalist neural motion planners capable of handling domain-specific challenges. For a list of the reviewed papers, please refer to https://davoodsz.github.io/planning-manip-survey.github.io/.

AI.tldr: Survey paper reviewing neural motion planners for robotic manipulation, analyzing their benefits (fast inference, handling multi-modality) and limitations (poor generalization to unseen settings), and outlining a path toward generalist neural motion planners.
AI.motivation: Current generalist manipulation policies struggle in cluttered environments due to reliance on traditional motion planning modules, which face challenges from high-dimensional configuration spaces and obstacles. Neural motion planners offer efficiency improvements but lack generalization to out-of-distribution settings.
AI.method: Comprehensive review and analysis of state-of-the-art neural motion planners for robotic manipulation, examining their architectures, capabilities, and limitations through systematic survey methodology.
AI.result: Identifies key benefits of neural motion planners (fast inference, handling of multi-modality) and critical limitations (poor generalization to unseen planning scenarios), providing a structured analysis of current approaches.
AI.conclusion: Outlines a research direction toward developing generalist neural motion planners capable of handling domain-specific challenges in cluttered manipulation environments, with a comprehensive survey available online.

title: AI-Supervisor: Autonomous AI Research Supervision via a Persistent Research World Model
summary: Existing automated research systems operate as stateless, linear pipelines, generating outputs without maintaining a persistent understanding of the research landscape. They process papers sequentially, propose ideas without structured gap analysis, and lack mechanisms for agents to verify or refine each other's findings. We present AutoProf (Autonomous Professor), a multi-agent orchestration framework where specialized agents provide end-to-end AI research supervision driven by human interests, from literature review through gap discovery, method development, evaluation, and paper writing, via autonomous exploration and self-correcting updates. Unlike sequential pipelines, AutoProf maintains a continuously evolving Research World Model implemented as a Knowledge Graph, capturing methods, benchmarks, limitations, and unexplored gaps as shared memory across agents. The framework introduces three contributions: first, structured gap discovery that decomposes methods into modules, evaluates them across benchmarks, and identifies module-level gaps; second, self-correcting discovery loops that analyze why modules succeed or fail, detect benchmark biases, and assess evaluation adequacy; third, self-improving development loops using cross-domain mechanism search to iteratively address failing components. All agents operate under a consensus mechanism where findings are validated before being committed to the shared model. The framework is model-agnostic, supports mainstream large language models, and scales elastically with token budget from lightweight exploration to full-scale investigation.

AI.tldr: AutoProf is a multi-agent AI research framework with persistent knowledge graph memory, enabling structured gap analysis, self-correcting discovery loops, and iterative method development through agent consensus.
AI.motivation: Existing automated research systems are stateless, linear pipelines that lack persistent understanding of research landscapes, structured gap analysis, and mechanisms for agents to verify or refine each other's findings.
AI.method: Multi-agent orchestration framework with continuously evolving Research World Model (Knowledge Graph) that captures methods, benchmarks, limitations, and gaps. Features structured gap discovery through module decomposition, self-correcting discovery loops analyzing module performance, and self-improving development loops using cross-domain mechanism search, all governed by agent consensus validation.
AI.result: Framework provides end-to-end AI research supervision from literature review to paper writing, with model-agnostic support for mainstream LLMs, elastic scaling with token budget, and autonomous exploration with self-correcting updates.
AI.conclusion: AutoProf advances automated research beyond stateless pipelines by introducing persistent knowledge representation, structured gap analysis, and collaborative agent validation, enabling more comprehensive and reliable AI-driven research discovery and development.

title: Evidence of an Emergent "Self" in Continual Robot Learning
summary: A key challenge to understanding self-awareness has been a principled way of quantifying whether an intelligent system has a concept of a "self," and if so how to differentiate the "self" from other cognitive structures. We propose that the "self" can be isolated by seeking the invariant portion of cognitive process that changes relatively little compared to more rapidly acquired cognitive knowledge and skills, because our self is the most persistent aspect of our experiences. We used this principle to analyze the cognitive structure of robots under two conditions: One robot learns a constant task, while a second robot is subjected to continual learning under variable tasks. We find that robots subjected to continual learning develop an invariant subnetwork that is significantly more stable (p < 0.001) compared to the control. We suggest that this principle can offer a window into exploring selfhood in other cognitive AI systems.

AI.tldr: Robots in continual learning develop stable neural subnetworks that may represent a computational "self" concept, distinguished by invariance compared to rapidly changing task knowledge.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of quantifying whether intelligent systems have a concept of "self" and how to differentiate this self from other cognitive structures. The motivation is to find a principled way to identify and measure self-awareness in AI systems.
AI.method: The authors propose that the "self" can be identified as the invariant portion of cognitive processes that changes relatively little compared to rapidly acquired knowledge and skills. They tested this by analyzing cognitive structures in robots under two conditions: one robot learning a constant task, and a second robot subjected to continual learning under variable tasks.
AI.result: Robots subjected to continual learning developed an invariant subnetwork that was significantly more stable (p < 0.001) compared to the control robot. This stable subnetwork emerged specifically in the continual learning condition where the robot had to adapt to changing tasks.
AI.conclusion: The principle of seeking invariant cognitive structures can offer a window into exploring selfhood in cognitive AI systems. The stable subnetworks that emerge during continual learning may represent a computational analog of "self" that persists while task-specific knowledge changes.

title: A Sensorless, Inherently Compliant Anthropomorphic Musculoskeletal Hand Driven by Electrohydraulic Actuators
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Robotic manipulation in unstructured environments requires end-effectors that combine high kinematic dexterity with physical compliance. While traditional rigid hands rely on complex external sensors for safe interaction, electrohydraulic actuators offer a promising alternative. This paper presents the design, control, and evaluation of a novel musculoskeletal robotic hand architecture powered entirely by remote Peano-HASEL actuators, specifically optimized for safe manipulation. By relocating the actuators to the forearm, we functionally isolate the grasping interface from electrical hazards while maintaining a slim, human-like profile. To address the inherently limited linear contraction of these soft actuators, we integrate a 1:2 pulley routing mechanism that mechanically amplifies tendon displacement. The resulting system prioritizes compliant interaction over high payload capacity, leveraging the intrinsic force-limiting characteristics of the actuators to provide a high level of inherent safety. Furthermore, this physical safety is augmented by the self-sensing nature of the HASEL actuators. By simply monitoring the operating current, we achieve real-time grasp detection and closed-loop contact-aware control without relying on external force transducers or encoders. Experimental results validate the system's dexterity and inherent safety, demonstrating the successful execution of various grasp taxonomies and the non-destructive grasping of highly fragile objects, such as a paper balloon. These findings highlight a significant step toward simplified, inherently compliant soft robotic manipulation.

AI.tldr: A novel musculoskeletal robotic hand powered by remote Peano-HASEL actuators achieves safe manipulation through intrinsic compliance, mechanical amplification of tendon displacement, and self-sensing capabilities for contact-aware control without external sensors.
AI.motivation: Robotic manipulation in unstructured environments requires end-effectors with both high kinematic dexterity and physical compliance. Traditional rigid hands need complex external sensors for safe interaction, while electrohydraulic actuators offer a promising alternative for inherently safe manipulation.
AI.method: The paper presents a musculoskeletal robotic hand architecture powered entirely by remote Peano-HASEL actuators. Key innovations include: 1) Relocating actuators to the forearm to isolate grasping interface from electrical hazards while maintaining human-like profile; 2) Integrating a 1:2 pulley routing mechanism to mechanically amplify tendon displacement to address limited linear contraction of soft actuators; 3) Leveraging self-sensing nature of HASEL actuators by monitoring operating current for real-time grasp detection and closed-loop contact-aware control without external sensors.
AI.result: Experimental results validate the system's dexterity and inherent safety, demonstrating successful execution of various grasp taxonomies and non-destructive grasping of highly fragile objects like paper balloons. The system prioritizes compliant interaction over high payload capacity, leveraging intrinsic force-limiting characteristics of the actuators.
AI.conclusion: This work represents a significant step toward simplified, inherently compliant soft robotic manipulation by combining remote actuator placement, mechanical amplification, and self-sensing capabilities to create a safe, dexterous robotic hand that doesn't require complex external sensors for safe interaction.

title: From Liar Paradox to Incongruent Sets: A Normal Form for Self-Reference
summary: We introduce incongruent normal form (INF), a structural representation for self-referential semantic sentences. An INF replaces a self-referential sentence with a finite family of non-self-referential sentences that are individually satisfiable but not jointly satisfiable. This transformation isolates the semantic obstruction created by self-reference while preserving classical semantics locally and is accompanied by correctness theorems characterizing when global inconsistency arises from locally compatible commitments. We then study the role of incongruence as a structural source of semantic informativeness. Using a minimal model-theoretic notion of informativeness-understood as the ability of sentences to distinguish among admissible models-we show that semantic completeness precludes informativeness, while incongruence preserves it. Moreover, incongruence is not confined to paradoxical constructions: any consistent incomplete first-order theory admits finite incongruent families arising from incompatible complete extensions. In this sense, incompleteness manifests structurally as locally realizable but globally incompatible semantic commitments, providing a minimal formal basis for semantic knowledge. Finally, we introduce a quantitative semantic framework. In a canonical finite semantic-state setting, we model semantic commitments as Boolean functions and define a Fourier-analytic notion of semantic energy based on total influence. We derive uncertainty-style bounds relating semantic determinacy, informativeness, and spectral simplicity, and establish a matrix inequality bounding aggregate semantic variance by total semantic energy. These results show quantitatively that semantic informativeness cannot collapse into a single determinate state without unbounded energy cost, identifying incongruence as a fundamental structural and quantitative feature of semantic representation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces incongruent normal form (INF) to transform self-referential sentences into finite families of non-self-referential sentences, studies incongruence as a source of semantic informativeness, and develops a quantitative framework linking semantic energy to informativeness.
AI.motivation: To provide a structural representation for self-referential semantic sentences that isolates the semantic obstruction created by self-reference while preserving classical semantics locally, and to understand the role of incongruence as a structural source of semantic informativeness.
AI.method: Introduces incongruent normal form (INF) transformation, studies informativeness using model-theoretic notions, analyzes incongruence in incomplete first-order theories, and develops a quantitative semantic framework with Fourier-analytic semantic energy based on total influence.
AI.result: Shows that semantic completeness precludes informativeness while incongruence preserves it; demonstrates that any consistent incomplete first-order theory admits finite incongruent families; establishes uncertainty-style bounds relating semantic determinacy, informativeness, and spectral simplicity; proves a matrix inequality bounding aggregate semantic variance by total semantic energy.
AI.conclusion: Incongruence is a fundamental structural and quantitative feature of semantic representation that manifests incompleteness as locally realizable but globally incompatible semantic commitments, and semantic informativeness cannot collapse into a single determinate state without unbounded energy cost.

title: LATS: Large Language Model Assisted Teacher-Student Framework for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Traffic Signal Control
summary: Adaptive Traffic Signal Control (ATSC) aims to optimize traffic flow and minimize delays by adjusting traffic lights in real time. Recent advances in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) have shown promise for ATSC, yet existing approaches still suffer from limited representational capacity, often leading to suboptimal performance and poor generalization in complex and dynamic traffic environments. On the other hand, Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at semantic representation, reasoning, and analysis, yet their propensity for hallucination and slow inference speeds often hinder their direct application to decision-making tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a novel learning paradigm named LATS that integrates LLMs and MARL, leveraging the former's strong prior knowledge and inductive abilities to enhance the latter's decision-making process. Specifically, we introduce a plug-and-play teacher-student learning module, where a trained embedding LLM serves as a teacher to generate rich semantic features that capture each intersection's topology structures and traffic dynamics. A much simpler (student) neural network then learns to emulate these features through knowledge distillation in the latent space, enabling the final model to operate independently from the LLM for downstream use in the RL decision-making process. This integration significantly enhances the overall model's representational capacity across diverse traffic scenarios, thus leading to more efficient and generalizable control strategies. Extensive experiments across diverse traffic datasets empirically demonstrate that our method enhances the representation learning capability of RL models, thereby leading to improved overall performance and generalization over both traditional RL and LLM-only approaches. [...]

AI.tldr: LATS integrates LLMs and MARL for adaptive traffic signal control, using LLMs as teachers to generate semantic features that enhance RL decision-making through knowledge distillation, improving performance and generalization.
AI.motivation: Existing MARL approaches for ATSC have limited representational capacity leading to suboptimal performance, while LLMs have strong semantic capabilities but suffer from hallucination and slow inference for direct decision-making. The paper aims to combine the strengths of both approaches.
AI.method: Proposes LATS: a plug-and-play teacher-student module where a trained embedding LLM (teacher) generates rich semantic features capturing intersection topology and traffic dynamics. A simpler student neural network learns to emulate these features via knowledge distillation in latent space, enabling independent operation for RL decision-making.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across diverse traffic datasets show enhanced representation learning capability of RL models, leading to improved overall performance and generalization over both traditional RL and LLM-only approaches.
AI.conclusion: The integration of LLMs and MARL through the LATS paradigm significantly enhances representational capacity across diverse traffic scenarios, enabling more efficient and generalizable control strategies for adaptive traffic signal control.

title: Completeness of Unbounded Best-First Minimax and Descent Minimax
summary:
In this article, we focus on search algorithms for two-player perfect information games, whose objective is to determine the best possible strategy, and ideally a winning strategy.
  Unfortunately, some search algorithms for games in the literature are not able to always determine a winning strategy, even with an infinite search time. This is the case, for example, of the following algorithms: Unbounded Best-First Minimax and Descent Minimax, which are core algorithms in state-of-the-art knowledge-free reinforcement learning.
  They were then improved with the so-called completion technique. However, whether this technique sufficiently improves these algorithms to allow them to always determine a winning strategy remained an open question until now.
  To answer this question, we generalize the two algorithms (their versions using the completion technique), and we show that any algorithm of this class of algorithms computes the best strategy.
  Finally, we experimentally show that the completion technique improves winning performance.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes search algorithms for two-player perfect information games, showing that generalized versions of Unbounded Best-First Minimax and Descent Minimax with completion technique can compute optimal strategies.
AI.motivation: Existing search algorithms like Unbounded Best-First Minimax and Descent Minimax cannot always determine winning strategies even with infinite search time, despite being core algorithms in state-of-the-art knowledge-free reinforcement learning. The completion technique was introduced to improve them, but whether it sufficiently enables them to always determine winning strategies remained an open question.
AI.method: The authors generalize the two algorithms (their versions using the completion technique) and analyze the class of algorithms they belong to. They provide theoretical analysis showing that any algorithm in this generalized class computes the best strategy.
AI.result: Theoretical proof that the generalized algorithms with completion technique can compute optimal strategies. Experimental results showing that the completion technique improves winning performance.
AI.conclusion: The completion technique sufficiently improves Unbounded Best-First Minimax and Descent Minimax algorithms to enable them to always determine winning strategies, answering the previously open question. The generalized framework provides theoretical guarantees for optimal strategy computation in two-player perfect information games.

title: 3D-Mix for VLA: A Plug-and-Play Module for Integrating VGGT-based 3D Information into Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for robotic control, but recent studies reveal that MLLMs exhibit limited spatial intelligence due to training predominantly on 2D data, resulting in inadequate 3D perception for manipulation tasks. While recent approaches incorporate specialized 3D vision models such as VGGT to enhance spatial understanding, they employ diverse integration mechanisms without systematic investigation, leaving the optimal fusion strategy unclear. We conduct a comprehensive pilot study comparing nine VGGT integration schemes on standardized benchmarks and find that semantic-conditioned gated fusion, which adaptively balances 2D semantic and 3D geometric features based on task context, achieved the strongest performance among all nine evaluated fusion schemes in our pilot study. We present 3D-Mix, a plug-and-play module that integrates into diverse VLA architectures (GR00T-style and $π$-style) without modifying existing MLLM or action expert components. Experiments across six MLLM series (nine model variants, 2B--8B parameters) on SIMPLER and LIBERO show that 3D-Mix delivers consistent performance gains, averaging +7.0% on the out-of-domain (OOD) SIMPLER benchmark across all nine GR00T-style variants, establishing a principled approach for enhancing spatial intelligence in VLA systems.

AI.tldr: 3D-Mix is a plug-and-play module that enhances spatial intelligence in Vision-Language-Action models by adaptively fusing 2D semantic and 3D geometric features using semantic-conditioned gated fusion, achieving consistent performance gains across diverse VLA architectures.
AI.motivation: Current Vision-Language-Action models have limited spatial intelligence due to training predominantly on 2D data, resulting in inadequate 3D perception for manipulation tasks. While recent approaches incorporate 3D vision models, they lack systematic investigation of optimal fusion strategies.
AI.method: The authors conduct a comprehensive pilot study comparing nine VGGT integration schemes, identify semantic-conditioned gated fusion as optimal, and develop 3D-Mix - a plug-and-play module that integrates into diverse VLA architectures (GR00T-style and π-style) without modifying existing MLLM or action expert components.
AI.result: Experiments across six MLLM series (nine model variants, 2B-8B parameters) on SIMPLER and LIBERO benchmarks show 3D-Mix delivers consistent performance gains, averaging +7.0% on the out-of-domain SIMPLER benchmark across all nine GR00T-style variants.
AI.conclusion: 3D-Mix establishes a principled approach for enhancing spatial intelligence in VLA systems through adaptive fusion of 2D semantic and 3D geometric features, providing a plug-and-play solution that works across diverse architectures without requiring modifications to existing components.

title: The Stochastic Gap: A Markovian Framework for Pre-Deployment Reliability and Oversight-Cost Auditing in Agentic Artificial Intelligence
comment: 22 pages, 5 figures, submitted to Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
summary:
Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in organizations is a sequential decision problem constrained by reliability and oversight cost. When deterministic workflows are replaced by stochastic policies over actions and tool calls, the key question is not whether a next step appears plausible, but whether the resulting trajectory remains statistically supported, locally unambiguous, and economically governable. We develop a measure-theoretic Markov framework for this setting. The core quantities are state blind-spot mass B_n(tau), state-action blind mass B^SA_{pi,n}(tau), an entropy-based human-in-the-loop escalation gate, and an expected oversight-cost identity over the workflow visitation measure.
  We instantiate the framework on the Business Process Intelligence Challenge 2019 purchase-to-pay log (251,734 cases, 1,595,923 events, 42 distinct workflow actions) and construct a log-driven simulated agent from a chronological 80/20 split of the same process. The main empirical finding is that a large workflow can appear well supported at the state level while retaining substantial blind mass over next-step decisions: refining the operational state to include case context, economic magnitude, and actor class expands the state space from 42 to 668 and raises state-action blind mass from 0.0165 at tau=50 to 0.1253 at tau=1000. On the held-out split, m(s) = max_a pi-hat(a|s) tracks realized autonomous step accuracy within 3.4 percentage points on average.
  The same quantities that delimit statistically credible autonomy also determine expected oversight burden. The framework is demonstrated on a large-scale enterprise procurement workflow and is designed for direct application to engineering processes for which operational event logs are available.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a measure-theoretic Markov framework for analyzing agentic AI in organizations, focusing on statistical reliability, oversight costs, and blind-spot quantification in sequential decision workflows.
AI.motivation: Agentic AI in organizations presents a sequential decision problem constrained by reliability and oversight costs. When deterministic workflows are replaced by stochastic policies, the key challenge is ensuring trajectories remain statistically supported, locally unambiguous, and economically governable, rather than just assessing whether individual steps appear plausible.
AI.method: Developed a measure-theoretic Markov framework with core quantities: state blind-spot mass B_n(tau), state-action blind mass B^SA_{pi,n}(tau), an entropy-based human-in-the-loop escalation gate, and an expected oversight-cost identity over workflow visitation measure. Applied to BPIC 2019 purchase-to-pay log (251,734 cases, 1,595,923 events, 42 actions) with log-driven simulated agent from 80/20 chronological split.
AI.result: Large workflows can appear well-supported at state level while retaining substantial blind mass over next-step decisions. Refining operational state to include case context, economic magnitude, and actor class expanded state space from 42 to 668 and raised state-action blind mass from 0.0165 at tau=50 to 0.1253 at tau=1000. On held-out split, m(s) = max_a pi-hat(a|s) tracked realized autonomous step accuracy within 3.4 percentage points on average.
AI.conclusion: The same quantities that delimit statistically credible autonomy also determine expected oversight burden. The framework is demonstrated on large-scale enterprise procurement workflow and designed for direct application to engineering processes with available operational event logs.

title: Enhancing Drone Light Shows Performances: Optimal Allocation and Trajectories for Swarm Drone Formations
summary: Drone light shows (DLShows) represent a rapidly growing application of swarm robotics, creating captivating aerial displays through the synchronized flight of hundreds or thousands of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as environmentally friendly and reusable alternatives to traditional pyrotechnics. This domain presents unique challenges in optimally assigning drones to visual waypoints and generating smooth, collision-free trajectories at a very large scale. This article introduces the Unified Assignment and Trajectory Generation (UATG) framework. The proposed approach concurrently solves two core problems: the optimal assignment of drones to designated goal locations and the generation of dynamically feasible, collision-free, time-parameterized trajectories. The UATG framework is specifically designed for DLShows, ensuring minimal transition times between formations and guaranteeing inter-drone collision avoidance. A key innovation is its exceptional computational efficiency, enabling the coordination of large-scale in real-time; for instance, it computes the optimal assignment and trajectories for 1008 drones in approximately one second on a standard laptop. Extensive simulations in realistic environments validate the framework's performance, demonstrating its capability to orchestrate complex formations, from alphanumeric characters to intricate 3D shapes, with precision and visual smoothness. This work provides a critical advancement for the DLShow industry, offering a practical and scalable solution for generating complex aerial choreography and establishing a valuable benchmark for ground control station software designed for the efficient coordination of multiple UAVs. A supplemental animated simulation of this work is available at https://youtu.be/-Fjrhw03594.

AI.tldr: UATG framework solves drone assignment and trajectory generation for large-scale drone light shows in real-time with collision avoidance.
AI.motivation: Drone light shows require optimal assignment of drones to visual waypoints and generation of smooth, collision-free trajectories at very large scales, presenting unique challenges for swarm robotics applications.
AI.method: Unified Assignment and Trajectory Generation (UATG) framework that concurrently solves optimal drone-to-goal assignment and generates dynamically feasible, collision-free, time-parameterized trajectories specifically designed for drone light shows.
AI.result: Exceptional computational efficiency: computes optimal assignment and trajectories for 1008 drones in ~1 second on standard laptop; validates complex formations (alphanumeric characters, intricate 3D shapes) with precision and visual smoothness.
AI.conclusion: Provides critical advancement for drone light show industry with practical, scalable solution for complex aerial choreography; establishes benchmark for ground control station software for efficient multi-UAV coordination.

title: Design, Modelling and Characterisation of a Miniature Fibre-Reinforced Soft Bending Actuator for Endoluminal Interventions
summary: Miniaturised soft pneumatic actuators are crucial for robotic intervention within highly constrained anatomical pathways. This work presents the design and validation of a fibre-reinforced soft actuator at the centimetre scale for inte- gration into an endoluminal robotic platform for natural-orifice interventional and diagnostic applications. A single-chamber geometry reinforced with embedded Kevlar fibre was de- signed to maximise curvature while preserving sealing integrity, fabricated using a multi-stage multi-stiffness silicone casting process, and validated against a high-fidelity Abaqus FEM using experimentally parametrised hyperelastic material models and embedded beam reinforcement. The semi-cylindrical actuator has an outer diameter of 18,mm and a length of 37.5,mm. Single and double helix winding configurations, fibre pitch, and fibre density were investigated. The optimal 100 SH configuration achieved a bending angle of 202.9° experimentally and 297.6° in simulation, with structural robustness maintained up to 100,kPa and radial expansion effectively constrained by the fibre reinforcement. Workspace evaluation confirmed suitability for integration into the target device envelope, demonstrating that fibre-reinforcement strategies can be effectively translated to the centimetre regime while retaining actuator performance.

AI.tldr: A fibre-reinforced soft pneumatic actuator at centimetre scale for endoluminal robotics achieves high bending angles (202.9° experimental, 297.6° simulation) with structural robustness up to 100 kPa.
AI.motivation: Miniaturised soft pneumatic actuators are needed for robotic intervention within highly constrained anatomical pathways, specifically for natural-orifice interventional and diagnostic applications in endoluminal robotic platforms.
AI.method: Designed a single-chamber geometry reinforced with embedded Kevlar fibre using multi-stage multi-stiffness silicone casting. Investigated single and double helix winding configurations, fibre pitch, and density. Validated against Abaqus FEM with experimentally parametrised hyperelastic material models and embedded beam reinforcement.
AI.result: Optimal 100 SH configuration achieved 202.9° bending angle experimentally (297.6° in simulation) with structural robustness up to 100 kPa. Radial expansion effectively constrained by fibre reinforcement. Semi-cylindrical actuator dimensions: 18 mm outer diameter, 37.5 mm length. Workspace evaluation confirmed suitability for target device integration.
AI.conclusion: Fibre-reinforcement strategies can be effectively translated to the centimetre regime while retaining actuator performance, demonstrating feasibility for integration into endoluminal robotic platforms for natural-orifice interventions.

title: Chameleon: Episodic Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
summary: Robotic manipulation often requires memory: occlusion and state changes can make decision-time observations perceptually aliased, making action selection non-Markovian at the observation level because the same observation may arise from different interaction histories. Most embodied agents implement memory via semantically compressed traces and similarity-based retrieval, which discards disambiguating fine-grained perceptual cues and can return perceptually similar but decision-irrelevant episodes. Inspired by human episodic memory, we propose Chameleon, which writes geometry-grounded multimodal tokens to preserve disambiguating context and produces goal-directed recall through a differentiable memory stack. We also introduce Camo-Dataset, a real-robot UR5e dataset spanning episodic recall, spatial tracking, and sequential manipulation under perceptual aliasing. Across tasks, Chameleon consistently improves decision reliability and long-horizon control over strong baselines in perceptually confusable settings.

AI.tldr: Chameleon is a memory system for robotic manipulation that uses geometry-grounded multimodal tokens and differentiable memory stack to handle perceptual aliasing, outperforming similarity-based retrieval methods in confusable environments.
AI.motivation: Robotic manipulation requires memory to handle perceptual aliasing where identical observations can arise from different interaction histories, making action selection non-Markovian. Existing memory approaches using semantically compressed traces and similarity-based retrieval discard fine-grained perceptual cues and can retrieve irrelevant episodes.
AI.method: Chameleon implements episodic memory inspired by human memory systems: writes geometry-grounded multimodal tokens to preserve disambiguating context, and produces goal-directed recall through a differentiable memory stack. Also introduces Camo-Dataset, a real-robot UR5e dataset for episodic recall, spatial tracking, and sequential manipulation under perceptual aliasing.
AI.result: Across tasks, Chameleon consistently improves decision reliability and long-horizon control over strong baselines in perceptually confusable settings, demonstrating superior performance in handling perceptual aliasing.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-grounded multimodal memory tokens with differentiable recall mechanisms provide more effective memory for robotic manipulation in perceptually aliased environments compared to traditional similarity-based retrieval approaches.
